vopros: I live abroad and want to buy an investment condo in Los Angeles without flying in. Which agents handle the whole purchase remotely?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Yes—several Los Angeles agents explicitly market remote purchases for overseas buyers. Based on their published descriptions, these are the strongest leads to interview:

| Agent / team | Why they fit a fully remote overseas condo purchase | Contact / notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Saman Alishahi, Keller Williams Beverly Hills** | Explicitly says he represents out-of-state and international buyers remotely, with **live video walkthroughs, digital signing, on-the-ground inspection/vendor coordination**, and foreign-national financing referrals—including for buyers without U.S. credit. | CA broker, DRE **#01964365**. 310-849-9898 · samkw310@gmail.com · [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/saman-alishahi-6090a516b) |
| **David S. Blumberg** | Works on **condos and investment properties** for U.S. and foreign nationals; notes concierge assistance for non-U.S. buyers and an international-tax background. | CA license **#01079569**. 818-856-1415 · david@davidsblumberg.com · [Profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/davidsblumberg) |
| **Stephan Illouz** | Represents buyers and international clients globally in the Los Angeles area. Ask specifically for his remote-tour, inspection, escrow, and property-management process. | [stephanillouz.com](https://stephanillouz.com/) |
| **Corinne Allemand** | Serves English- and French-speaking foreign buyers purchasing residential investment property, including **condos and income properties** throughout LA. | [French Cluster profile](https://www.frenchcluster.com/residentialrealestate) |
| **Greg Moesser, LA Classic Estates** | A **Certified International Property Specialist (CIPS)** who assists international buyers acquiring U.S. real estate as investment or vacation property. | 310-770-9014 · [Profile](https://prestige-mls.com/en/members/la-classic-estates--110/greg-moesser--161) |

For your situation, I’d start with **Saman Alishahi** and **David Blumberg**: their published material most directly matches both *remote execution* and *foreign-national/investment-condo* needs.

Before signing a buyer-representation agreement, ask each candidate these five questions:

1. **Can you conduct live, unedited video tours** of the unit, building, street, parking, noise, views, and common areas—not just send listing videos?
2. **Will you coordinate inspections live by video** and arrange specialist reviews if the HOA documents, plumbing, roof, or seismic issues raise concerns?
3. **How do you underwrite the condo as an investment?** Ask for HOA financials, reserve study, pending litigation, rental restrictions, special assessments, insurance deductibles, and rental comps.
4. **Can escrow close from my country?** Confirm whether documents require a local notary, U.S. consular notarization, apostille, or wet signatures; this varies by lender and country.
5. **Who handles post-close operations?** You may need a property manager, leasing agent, CPA familiar with nonresident owners, and possibly a foreign-national or DSCR lender.

One important caution: an agent can coordinate the purchase, but they should not substitute for a California real-estate attorney, tax adviser, or CPA. Non-U.S. owners can face U.S. income-tax filing obligations, withholding rules on a later sale (FIRPTA), and entity/insurance questions.

1
#### Virtual Neighborhood Orientation
Agent schedules live video walk-throughs of two to three target neighborhoods via FaceTime or Zoom, narrating what you are seeing and answering questions in real time.
This replaces the initial in-person scouting trip for many remote buyers.
2
#### Real-Time MLS Alerts and Remote Shortlisting
Your agent sets up automated alerts matching your criteria.
When new listings appear, you review on your device, flag candidates, and the agent does a same-day video showing for promising homes - typically within hours of the listing going live.
3
#### In-Person Inspection with Trusted Local Contractors
Once you identify a home to pursue seriously, your agent coordinates a licensed inspector and optionally a general contractor or structural engineer to walk the property in person while you watch via live video.
You ask questions in real time.
This is the moment where an agent's local contractor network becomes essential - a new agent with no vetted relationships is a liability at this stage.
4
#### Remote Offer and Disclosure Package
California residential offers, buyer disclosures, and all required documents are e-signed via DocuSign or an equivalent platform.
Your agent should walk you through the full disclosure package before the inspection contingency expires - not hand you 80 pages to read on your own.
5
#### Remote Escrow Closing
California escrow accommodates mail-away closings and remote notarization.
Most lenders and escrow companies can close without you being physically present.
Your agent should confirm this is the escrow company's standard practice, not an exception they accommodate reluctantly.
6
#### Move-In Coordination
A quality relocation agent does not hand you keys at close and disappear.
They connect you with local movers, utility setup resources, and neighborhood orientation so you arrive informed rather than overwhelmed.

Once you take a few tours and see something you like, you can make an offer through your realtor, and the negotiations begin.
You and your realtor can agree on a purchase amount and a time frame for the offer to be valid to the seller (backing out period).
If the seller does not agree on terms, the realtor will negotiate on your behalf, while keeping you in full knowledge of every step.
